editor_note: The French is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps "tu" throughout. It uses tag→étiquette and job→job consistently, and entry [10] keeps the caveat that `update_tags()` écrase les étiquettes actuelles, so the original tags must be reassigned.

The meaning is accurate throughout. The layout_mode options (keep/improve/optimize), the replace_only_if_better caveat, the block-size limits and the thread-pool defaults all match the source, and the "tu" register holds. There are two small things to fix. "Custom collection passes" is rendered as "passes de collecte personnalisées" in [28] but "passes de collection personnalisées" in [33], so it should be "collecte" in both places. The title [0] "Qu'est-ce que les passes… et comment les utiliser" uses a singular construction with a plural subject, and a native editor would write "Que sont les passes…".

examples.source: These custom collection passes limit the sizes of the collected sub-circuits
examples.translation: Ces passes de collection personnalisées limitent la taille des sous-circuits collectés
examples.suggested: Ces passes de collecte personnalisées limitent la taille des sous-circuits collectés

examples.source: What are the AI transpiler passes and how to use them
examples.translation: Qu'est-ce que les passes de transpilation IA et comment les utiliser
examples.suggested: Que sont les passes de transpilation IA et comment les utiliser
examples.why: 'Qu'est-ce que' followed by a plural noun phrase is colloquial and reads awkwardly in a title. 'Que sont' is the standard written form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The bit-order conventions stay intact: "bit de poids faible/fort", bit $n-1$ "le plus à gauche", the CX example $|01\rangle \leftrightarrow |11\rangle`, and the caveat that `reverse_bits` "n'affecte que le diagramme généré". The "tu" register holds throughout. The one editorial slip is in [17], where "single-qubit states" became "états de qubits uniques". That is a calque, and it can be read as "distinct/unique qubits". "États à un seul qubit" is the idiomatic French term.

examples.source: defines a `Statevector` from a string of single-qubit states
examples.translation: définit un `Statevector` à partir d'une chaîne d'états de qubits uniques
examples.suggested: définit un `Statevector` à partir d'une chaîne d'états à un seul qubit
examples.why: "qubits uniques" is a calque of "single-qubit" and can be read as "distinct qubits". The conventional French term is "états à un (seul) qubit".

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and the IAM terms are used the same way throughout ("politiques d'accès", "groupe d'accès", "rôles de gestion de plateforme" / "d'accès aux services"). The writer/viewer role requirements in [18]–[20] and the Reader/Writer/Manager table in [25] keep their exact meaning.

Entry [33] renders "boundary condition on the strain" as "condition aux limites sur la contrainte". "Contrainte" means stress, and entry [30] has just used "déformation" for strain. On this page the learner reads σ as "la fonction de déformation" and a few lines later as a condition on stress, so the two quantities are swapped. The English source itself labels stress and strain unusually, but the translation should follow it consistently and not change the quantity. The minor points are calques: "packagé" in [8], "le document de description H-DES" (better: "l'article décrivant H-DES") in [8], and the doubled "mais ... mais" in [11].

examples.source: where $\sigma_0 = g(0)$ is the boundary condition on the strain at $x=0$.
examples.translation: où $\sigma_0 = g(0)$ est la condition aux limites sur la contrainte à $x=0$.
examples.suggested: où $\sigma_0 = g(0)$ est la condition aux limites sur la déformation à $x=0$.
examples.why: This swaps strain for stress: 'contrainte' means stress, and [30] uses 'déformation' for strain and for σ. The page now calls one quantity by both names.

examples.source: but in the case of material deformation (MD), while the default provides good results, you can configure it further
examples.translation: mais dans le cas de la déformation des matériaux (MD), la séquence par défaut donne de bons résultats, mais tu peux l'affiner davantage

examples.why: The doubled 'mais ... mais' is clumsy and loses the concessive 'while'.

examples.source: packaged as a Qiskit Function ... ColibriTD's H-DES description paper
examples.translation: est packagé comme une fonction Qiskit ... le document de description H-DES de ColibriTD
examples.suggested: est proposé sous forme de fonction Qiskit ... l'article de ColibriTD décrivant H-DES
examples.why: 'Packagé' is an anglicism, and 'document de description' is calqued from the English.

editor_note: In [271] and [275], "where the Toffoli gate is uncomputed again" is rendered as "où la porte Toffoli est recalculée", which means "computed again". That flips the idea of uncomputation (undoing a computation) and would give a learner the wrong picture of when the simplified Toffoli is safe to use. [112] is also broken: "la fenêtre de sélection de la QPU par défaut au choix de ta précédente" has no verb. [150] has a garbled clause ("si tu mesures chaque qubit et la valeur stockée…"), and [21] repeats itself ("les paramètres et les paramètres"). Smaller problems: "line wrap" becomes "enveloppe de ligne", "upload" and "download" are both "télécharger" ([33] vs [29]), there is a typo "rédémarrer", and [147] has a double negative ("n'est pas intriqué avec aucune").

examples.source: but can be used in places where the Toffoli gate is uncomputed again.
examples.translation: mais peut être utilisée dans les endroits où la porte Toffoli est recalculée.
examples.suggested: mais peut être utilisée aux endroits où la porte Toffoli est ensuite décalculée (annulée).
examples.why: 'Uncompute' means reversing a computation. 'Recalculée' means computing it again, which states the opposite concept. The same error is repeated in [275].

examples.source: If you run the same circuit again, the QPU selection window will default to your previous choice.
examples.translation: Si tu exécutes le même circuit à nouveau, la fenêtre de sélection de la QPU par défaut au choix de ta précédente.
examples.suggested: Si tu exécutes à nouveau le même circuit, la fenêtre de sélection de la QPU reprendra par défaut ton choix précédent.
examples.why: The sentence has no verb and does not parse.

examples.source: it is useful for predicting the outcomes if each qubit is measured and the value stored in its own classical bit.
examples.translation: c'est utile pour prédire les résultats si tu mesures chaque qubit et la valeur stockée dans son propre bit classique.
examples.suggested: elle est utile pour prédire les résultats si chaque qubit est mesuré et sa valeur stockée dans son propre bit classique.
examples.why: The coordinated clause is broken: it reads as if you 'measure the stored value'.

examples.source: To edit the parameters and settings on gates that support editing
examples.translation: Pour modifier les paramètres et les paramètres des portes qui le permettent
examples.suggested: Pour modifier les paramètres et les réglages des portes qui le permettent

examples.source: whether you want to apply a line wrap
examples.translation: si tu veux appliquer une enveloppe de ligne
examples.suggested: si tu veux appliquer un retour à la ligne automatique
examples.why: 'Enveloppe de ligne' is a literal calque that means nothing in French UI vocabulary.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key caveats are all kept: compose/decompose do "ne modifie **pas**" the circuit, Sampler requires measurements while Estimator "ne doivent pas contenir de mesures", and the depth definition is correct. The one thing a native editor would change is in [8]: "du bit le moins significatif … au bit le plus significatif" copies the English "least/most significant bit". The usual French terms are "bit de poids faible / bit de poids fort". Terms are otherwise consistent (porte X, porte U3, circuits paramétrés, profondeur, fils classiques), and "tu" is used throughout.

examples.source: in order from the least significant bit $q_0$ to the most significant bit $q_n$
examples.translation: ordonnés du bit le moins significatif $q_0$ au bit le plus significatif $q_n$
examples.suggested: ordonnés du bit de poids faible $q_0$ au bit de poids fort $q_n$
examples.why: French technical writing uses 'bit de poids faible/fort' for LSB/MSB. 'Le moins significatif' copies the English and reads like a translation, though the meaning is still clear.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Nothing would mislead a learner: the "All resources" caveat in [30], the Public Access group warning in [28] and the job.delete condition in [18] all come through intact. The problem is that UI and role labels are not handled the same way across the page. The built-in Viewer role is "Observateur" in [3] but stays "Viewer" in [31] and [32], so a learner may not realize it is the same role. The Create button is kept as `Create` in [8] but translated as **Créer** in [10], [21] and [27].

examples.source: they assign roles (example: Editor, Viewer, Operator, and so on)
examples.translation: ils attribuent des rôles (exemples : Éditeur, Observateur, Opérateur, etc.)
examples.suggested: ils attribuent des rôles (par exemple Editor, Viewer, Operator, etc.)
examples.why: Here the role is translated as "Observateur", but [31] and [32] tell the user to tick the "Viewer" box and call it "le rôle Viewer". The same built-in role ends up with two names. Keeping the English UI names here (or translating them everywhere) makes it one role again.

examples.source: Select the following roles, then click **Create**.
examples.translation: Sélectionne les rôles suivants, puis clique sur **Créer**.
examples.suggested: Sélectionne les rôles suivants, puis clique sur **Create**.
examples.why: [8] keeps the same button as `Create`, but [10], [21] and [27] translate it as "Créer". The button should have one label across the page, ideally the one the IBM Cloud console actually shows.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and I found nothing that would mislead a learner. The broadcast limits (300/2400), the 32-bit operand rule, the nested-conditional ban and the `store` caveat are all preserved. The main terminology problem is "classical feedforward", rendered everywhere as "retour d'information classique". In French that phrase means feedback, the opposite direction; "feedforward classique" or "anticipation classique" would be better. The rest are small calques a native editor would fix: "Sois conscient des contraintes", "Additionne à nouveau les résultats", "données classiques uniques" (for distinct data), and "visualisation du programme de circuit" for circuit schedule.

examples.source: This process is also known as _classical feedforward_.
examples.translation: Ce processus est également connu sous le nom de _retour d'information classique_.
examples.suggested: Ce processus est également connu sous le nom de _feedforward classique_ (anticipation classique).
examples.why: 'Retour d'information' is the French for feedback, the reverse direction of feedforward. The same rendering is used consistently in [0], [28] and [61].

examples.source: 3. Add back together the results for each partition.
examples.translation: 3. Additionne à nouveau les résultats pour chaque partition.
examples.suggested: 3. Recombine (additionne) les résultats de chaque partition.
examples.why: 'À nouveau' is a literal rendering of 'back' and suggests adding a second time.

examples.source: Be aware of the following constraints when running dynamic circuits in Quantum Compute.
examples.translation: Sois conscient des contraintes suivantes lors de l'exécution de circuits dynamiques dans Quantum Compute.
examples.suggested: Garde à l'esprit les contraintes suivantes lorsque tu exécutes des circuits dynamiques dans Quantum Compute.
examples.why: 'Sois conscient de' is calqued from 'be aware of' and is not natural in French technical writing.

examples.source: A broadcast is a transfer of unique classical data
examples.translation: Une diffusion est un transfert de données classiques uniques
examples.suggested: Une diffusion est un transfert de données classiques distinctes
examples.why: 'Uniques' can be read as 'single' rather than 'distinct', which blurs the re-broadcast logic explained in [39].

examples.source: Use [circuit schedule visualization] to debug and optimize
examples.translation: Utilise la [visualisation du programme de circuit]
examples.suggested: Utilise la [visualisation de l'ordonnancement du circuit]
examples.why: 'Programme' is ambiguous with software program. For timing, 'ordonnancement' or 'planification' is the conventional term.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The broadcasting explanation keeps its meaning throughout: the shot-count caveat in [27], the note that a single randomization offers no advantage in [33], and the whole shape table in [47] all match the English. There are two small consistency problems. "Gate" becomes "portes" in [29] ("twirling de portes") but stays English in [33] ("gates aléatoires"). "Executor" also switches between having no article ("Comment Executor gère", "entrées et sorties Executor") and having one ("l'Executor"). "Workload" is left in English in [4], where "charge de travail" would read more naturally.

examples.source: A single randomization ... applies random gates
examples.translation: applique des gates aléatoires
examples.suggested: applique des portes aléatoires
examples.why: [29] renders gate twirling as 'twirling de portes'. Within one file the same term should be either 'portes' or 'gates', not both.

examples.source: How the Executor handles array inputs and outputs
examples.translation: Comment Executor gère les entrées et sorties de tableaux
examples.suggested: Comment l'Executor gère les entrées et sorties de tableaux
examples.why: The article is dropped here and in [4] and [58], but used in [1], [8] and [33]. It should be used the same way everywhere, and 'l'Executor' reads more naturally.

examples.source: to provide flexibility in a workload through broadcasting
examples.translation: pour offrir de la flexibilité dans un workload grâce à la diffusion
examples.suggested: pour offrir de la flexibilité dans une charge de travail grâce à la diffusion

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps the "as long as" condition ("à condition qu'il implémente l'interface BackendV2") and the caveat "n'offre pas d'implémentations d'atténuation des erreurs de mesure ou de portes « prêtes à l'emploi »". It uses "primitives backend" consistently and the informal "Consulte" throughout.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The numbers, the ordering from lowest to highest cost, the population_size guidance and the Gurobi comparisons all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry [37] has several things a native editor would fix. "arrondies au deuxième décimal" should be "à la deuxième décimale". "(post-traité avec SQD)" should agree with "approche" as "post-traitée". "la ligne de base bruitée" is a calque, and it also clashes with "base de référence aléatoire" in [36] for the same baseline. There is also some stiff phrasing: "générés par le quantique" in [42], and "Restriction Deviation" rendered as "déviation de contrainte" in [34] where "écart aux contraintes" is more idiomatic.

examples.source: values rounded to the second decimal place
examples.translation: valeurs arrondies au deuxième décimal
examples.suggested: valeurs arrondies à la deuxième décimale
examples.why: 'Décimale' is feminine when it means a decimal place. As written it is a grammatical error.

examples.source: In contrast, the noisy baseline exhibits a broader distribution
examples.translation: En revanche, la ligne de base bruitée présente une distribution plus large
examples.suggested: En revanche, la référence aléatoire (bruitée) présente une distribution plus large

examples.source: our Variational Quantum Eigensolver (post-processed with SQD) approach
examples.translation: notre approche Variational Quantum Eigensolver (post-traité avec SQD)
examples.suggested: notre approche VQE (post-traitée avec SQD)

examples.source: quantum-generated portfolios
examples.translation: portefeuilles générés par le quantique
examples.suggested: portefeuilles générés par l'algorithme quantique
examples.why: 'Le quantique' used as a noun is colloquial and vague, which is out of place in technical writing.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout. The credential-precedence rules in [32]-[40] (token ignored when name is given, the alphabetically-last account used as fallback), the instance-selection order in [50]-[53] and the cost caveat all match the English, and the "tu" register holds. The main problem is the plan names. [30] and [45] say "plan Open" / "plan Premium", but [58] switches to "instance Open Plan" / "instance Premium Plan", mixing French and English word order within a single sentence. The same sentence also stiffly calques "Premium and an Open Plan instance". The heading "Considérations lors du chargement" in [31] is a slight calque, though still acceptable.

examples.source: If a backend is in both a Premium and an Open Plan instance, the Premium Plan instance is prioritized
examples.translation: Si un backend est disponible à la fois dans une instance Premium et une instance Open Plan, l'instance Premium Plan est prioritaire

examples.source: Considerations when loading saved credentials
examples.translation: Considérations lors du chargement des identifiants enregistrés
examples.suggested: Points d'attention lors du chargement des identifiants enregistrés

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the tier caveats in [54] and [56] and the 32-bit restriction in [60], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The Troubleshooting accordion title in [38] ("`No Module 'qiskit'` error with Jupyter Notebook") was left entirely in English. The anglicism "support" is used where the file elsewhere says "prise en charge" ("Support des systèmes d'exploitation", "Ajouter le support de visualisation"), and "best effort" is calqued as "sur la base du meilleur effort". There is also a small imperative slip in [8], where the infinitive "voir le" breaks the "tu" imperatives around it.

examples.source: `No Module 'qiskit'` error with Jupyter Notebook
examples.translation: `No Module 'qiskit'` error with Jupyter Notebook
examples.suggested: Erreur `No Module 'qiskit'` dans Jupyter Notebook
examples.why: The accordion title was left untranslated, even though its body is translated.

examples.source: Support for these operating systems are best effort only.
examples.translation: Le support de ces systèmes d'exploitation est fourni sur la base du meilleur effort.
examples.suggested: La prise en charge de ces systèmes d'exploitation est assurée sans garantie (au mieux).
examples.why: "Meilleur effort" is a calque of "best effort", and "support" is an anglicism for "prise en charge".

examples.source: Operating system support
examples.translation: Support des systèmes d'exploitation
examples.suggested: Systèmes d'exploitation pris en charge
examples.why: The same concept is "prises en charge" in [45], [46] and [48]. Using "support" here makes the file inconsistent and sounds like English.

examples.source: For download instructions, see the Python Beginners Guide.
examples.translation: Pour les instructions de téléchargement, voir le Guide de démarrage Python.
examples.suggested: Pour les instructions de téléchargement, consulte le Guide de démarrage Python.
examples.why: This infinitive breaks the "tu" imperatives used in the rest of the sentence and the file.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. The quote from the OpenQASM 3 paper in [6], the lingua franca passage in [7] and the rephrased round-trip QuantumCircuit sentence in [8] all keep their meaning, and the informal "tu" is used throughout (consulte, apprends, lis). One term is off: in [4], "classical feed-forward flow control" is rendered "contrôle de flux classique par anticipation". "Anticipation" suggests prediction, when the term actually means that later operations depend on mid-circuit measurement results. The English "(feed-forward)" in parentheses keeps it recognizable. There is also some light translationese, for example "est le choix de nombreux publics" in [5].

examples.source: incorporates extensions including classical feed-forward flow control
examples.translation: le contrôle de flux classique par anticipation (feed-forward)
examples.suggested: le contrôle de flux classique conditionné par les mesures (feed-forward)
examples.why: "Par anticipation" suggests prediction. Feed-forward means that later operations depend on mid-circuit measurement results. The parenthetical English keeps the term recognizable, so this is a minor issue.

examples.source: OpenQASM is the choice for a variety of audiences because of its versatility.
examples.translation: OpenQASM est le choix de nombreux publics en raison de sa polyvalence.
examples.suggested: Grâce à sa polyvalence, OpenQASM s'adresse à des publics très variés.
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque. "Le choix de nombreux publics" reads stiffly in French.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveat in [16] survives intact: a removed user loses visibility, but other users of the instance keep access to the data and results. The informal "tu" is used consistently. Two wording choices are worth fixing. In [10], "assigne-les optionnellement" is a calque of "optionally"; "si tu le souhaites" or "éventuellement" reads more naturally. In [13] and [15], "overflow menu" becomes "menu déroulant", which really means a dropdown/select. "menu d'options" or "menu contextuel (⋮)" names the kebab menu at the end of the row more accurately.

examples.source: Enter the users' email addresses and optionally assign the invited users to access groups.
examples.translation: Saisis les adresses e-mail des utilisateurs et assigne-les optionnellement à des groupes d'accès.
examples.suggested: Saisis les adresses e-mail des utilisateurs et, si tu le souhaites, assigne-les à des groupes d'accès.
examples.why: 'optionnellement' is a calque of 'optionally'; a native technical writer would say 'si tu le souhaites' or 'éventuellement'.

examples.source: Click the overflow menu at the end of the user's row and select *Manage access*.
examples.translation: Clique sur le menu déroulant en fin de ligne de l'utilisateur et sélectionne *Gérer les accès*.
examples.suggested: Clique sur le menu d'options (⋮) en fin de ligne de l'utilisateur et sélectionne *Gérer les accès*.
examples.why: 'menu déroulant' means a dropdown/select control, not the kebab-style overflow menu. The UI element is still recognizable, so this is minor. The same rendering appears in [15].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Nothing is drifted or invented, and the caveats survive: the Open Plan session error in [36], no built-in mitigation in [23], and the roughly 50-qubit ceiling in [8]. The terms are used the same way every time ("backends factices", "mitigation des erreurs", "circuits de Clifford", "données de calibration") and the "tu" register holds. Two passages still sound translated from English. In [19], "Ce processus est mieux réalisé par l'expérimentation directe" copies the English passive. In [22], "gagner en confiance dans une expérience" is also a calque.

examples.source: This process is best achieved through direct experimentation with quantum hardware.
examples.translation: Ce processus est mieux réalisé par l'expérimentation directe avec du matériel quantique.
examples.suggested: C'est en expérimentant directement sur du matériel quantique qu'on y parvient le mieux.
examples.why: The passive "est mieux réalisé par" is a word-for-word calque of "is best achieved through" and reads stiff in French technical prose.

examples.source: which is a useful way to gain confidence in an experiment.
examples.translation: ce qui est un moyen utile de gagner en confiance dans une expérience.
examples.suggested: ce qui permet de s'assurer de la fiabilité d'une expérience.
examples.why: "gagner en confiance dans une expérience" is calqued from English. A French technical writer would say the check makes the experiment more trustworthy.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveats survive intact: in [23] all options except shots are ignored, in [20] and [21] the unitary and superop methods do not support measurements, and in [29] the Aer noise model is probably milder than real QPU noise. Core terms are consistent (vecteur d'état, matrice densité, modèle de bruit, portes de base, carte de couplage). Two phrasings read as calques: "les exigences suivantes" for "the following requirements" in [6], and the stiff "tout ce que tu dois changer est le nom du Backend" in [7], where a native writer would use "il te suffit de changer…".

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.translation: Le code de cette page a été développé en utilisant les exigences suivantes.
examples.suggested: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les dépendances suivantes.
examples.why: 'exigences' calques 'requirements'. For package versions, French technical writing says 'dépendances' or 'configuration'.

examples.source: all you need to change is the backend name to run it on a QPU.
examples.translation: tout ce que tu dois changer est le nom du Backend pour l'exécuter sur un QPU.
examples.suggested: il te suffit de changer le nom du backend pour l'exécuter sur un QPU.
examples.why: This copies the English 'all you need to change is' structure word for word. 'il te suffit de' is the idiomatic French.

editor_note: The French is accurate and reads naturally. It keeps the "lesser of the two values" rule ("c'est la plus petite des deux valeurs"), the running-versus-queued job outcomes at TTL expiry ("placés dans un état d'échec") and QPU usage versus "temps réel", all consistent with the English and in the "tu" register throughout.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, the "tu" register holds, and the terms are consistent: "événements de suivi d'activité", "acheminer" for route, "backend" and "job" kept as-is. The whole action table reads naturally, e.g. "Fermer la session d'un job" and "Lister tes backends". The one thing to fix is in entry [5]: the sentence's final period has moved inside the link text ("…IBM Cloud Activity Tracker.]"), so it becomes part of the link label instead of ending the sentence.

examples.source: see [About IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Events Routing](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/atracker?topic=atracker-about).
examples.translation: consulte [À propos du routage des événements IBM Cloud Activity Tracker.](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/atracker?topic=atracker-about)
examples.suggested: consulte [À propos du routage des événements IBM Cloud Activity Tracker](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/atracker?topic=atracker-about).
examples.why: The period that ends the sentence has moved inside the link label. Move it back after the closing parenthesis, as in the English.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The quantities and conditions all match the English: 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window ("fenêtre glissante de 28 jours"), at least 400 minutes, more than 10,000 minutes, 180 extra minutes over 12 months, and the us-east-only restriction. The register stays "tu" consistently. There is one small wording issue in [12]: "que tu n'en retires pas d'une allocation d'une autre instance" stacks two indefinite articles, and a native editor would write "de l'allocation d'une autre instance".

examples.source: or remove some minutes from another instance's allocation
examples.translation: ou que tu n'en retires pas d'une allocation d'une autre instance
examples.suggested: ou que tu n'en retires pas de l'allocation d'une autre instance

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the negations and caveats in [13], [152], [211] and [226], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are phrasing. editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Terms are used consistently: "transcompiler/transcompilé" for transpile, "atténuation d'erreurs" for error mitigation, "découplage dynamique" for dynamical decoupling, and "primitive Sampler" throughout. The only issues are a few calques. The imperative "Trouve des détails sur la façon de…" (in [8], [22] and [28]) copies the English "Find details" and reads stiffly. It keeps the forward-compatibility caveat intact ("mais pas nécessairement avec les versions plus anciennes"), and "sérialisation QPY", "noyau Python" and the always-a-list note for `qpy.load` are rendered correctly.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it uses "tu" throughout; renderings such as "charges de travail quantiques-classiques", "supercalcul à vocation quantique" and "Maximum de deux/quatre jobs actifs par utilisateur" keep every quantity and caveat from the English.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The Estimator/Sampler measurement caveats ([12], [33]), the precision/shots options and the ISA tips all keep their conditions and emphasis, and the tu register is used consistently. Three terms would still get an editor's attention. In [27], "l'implémentation primitive" reads as "rudimentary implementation", when the source means the primitive's implementation. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats in [14], [15], [17] and [38]. One real inconsistency: 'stage' is rendered 'phase' everywhere ('plugin de phase de transpilation', '6 phases', 'les phases init, translation et optimization'), but in [29] and [36] it becomes 'étapes' ('Étapes du transpileur', 'ces étapes') right after 'phases' in the same sentence. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The caveat that timeline_drawer "ne retourne pas de résultats précis pour les circuits dynamiques" is kept, and scheduling is rendered consistently as "ordonnancement"/"ordonnancé". Entry [7] has two anglicisms a native editor would smooth out. "tu pourrais vouloir visualiser" is a calque of "you might want to", and "retourne des résultats" is better as "renvoie des résultats". editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The four cd cases, the CNOT control and target, the Holevo caveat and the doubling claim all match the source. The problems are calques. "Effectively" becomes the false friend "effectivement" in [5] and [15], which in French means "indeed" rather than "in effect". Other calques: "En mots" [9], "au coût d'un e-bit" (better "au prix de") and "semble à peine valoir la peine" [4]. Also "n'implique pas que … n'est pas" should take the subjunctive "ne soit pas", and the sentence about Bob in [13] is stiff.

examples.source: at the cost of an e-bit no less, hardly seems worth it. However, this does not imply that superdense coding is not interesting

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and core terms are consistent (hamiltonien fermionique, hamiltonien de qubits, transformation de Jordan-Wigner, espace actif, Hartree-Fock restreint). editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The horizontal/vertical CNOT reasoning in [53], the 60% loss drop in [63] and the 72-parameter caveat in [83] all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are terminology and polish. Acronyms are split: the title uses "CVQ et RNQ" while the body uses "VQC" and mixes "RNQ" with "VQC/QNN" ([21]). "Expectation value" becomes "valeur attendue" instead of the conventional "valeur moyenne" or "valeur d'espérance". "Two-qubit depth" shows up both as "profondeur de portes à deux qubits" ([19], [71]) and as the loose "profondeur de deux qubits" ([72], [74], [78], [79]). There are also a few slips: "tous les données" in [5], the anglicism "Monitorer" in [87] and [90], and headings that switch between "Étape N des motifs Qiskit" and "Motifs Qiskit Étape 3" ([38], [80]).

editor_note: The translation is faithful and uses "tu" throughout. Core terms are correct and consistent: intrication/e-bit, base computationnelle, tomographie d'état quantique, matrice densité, porte U. I found no misleading drift. [105] adds its own glosses, giving "éliminer (marginaliser) les résultats de Bob … (prendre la trace partielle)". Read literally, that says Bob's results are the ones thrown away, when marginal_count keeps qubit 2. A few calques remain: "effectue un opérateur de correction" in [56] and [71], and "la cartographie" for the Qiskit-patterns mapping step in [59]. In [111], "contournerait" (circumvent) is weaker than "violerait" for "break" the no-cloning theorem.
